question: CReorgPanel and CReorgEntry read whole: the window two units hand brigades between - its constructor, the fill, the rows, transferbutton, the close, the keep-open test, the tooltips, the positioning penalty and the units ratio.

structs.name: CReorgPanel
structs.comment: The reorganise window (`reorg_window` of unitpanel.gui), the one the in-game screen keeps at +0x1358. Not polymorphic: no table of its own; the RTTI export knows it only by its CButtonObserverGlue<CReorgPanel> (vftable VA 0x15D99E8). Made once by CInGameIdler::Enter (`push 0x4C; call operator new` at 0x65F067, constructor at 0x65F08C). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.
structs.evidence: Size: Enter allocates 0x4C bytes (push 0x4C at 0x65F067) and the constructor's last field write is +0x48 (0x763ECD). No vftable is written at +0: +0 receives the made window (0x763DBA). What would show it wrong: a second allocation site with another size.

structs.name: CReorgEntry
structs.comment: One row of the reorganise window, `reorg_entry` in left_list or `reorg_entry_right` in right_list. RTTI base CStandardlistboxItem, a second table at +0x1C (VA 0x15D995C). Overrides only its two slot 0s (the destructors): its slot 8, the per-frame update of a list row, is the shared empty `ret` 0xABF890, so a row's figures are those of the moment it was made. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.
structs.evidence: Size: both makers `push 0xC8` (200) before operator new (0x770210's two sites), and the glue at +0x78 is 0x50 bytes (the glue constructor 0x76FBA0 writes EAX[0]..EAX[0x13]), ending at 0xC8. Table: the constructor writes 0x15D9924 to +0 and 0x15D995C to +0x1C at 0x763187/0x76318D; the RTTI export gives the same two (12 and 23 slots). Slot 8 of the primary table read as 0xABF890 off the table at VA 0x15D9924 + 0x20.

addresses.name: CReorgPanel::CReorgPanel
addresses.comment: **The reorganise window's constructor**, called once from CInGameIdler::Enter (0x65F08C) with the screen. Lays down the CButtonObserverGlue<CReorgPanel> at +0xC (vftable VA 0x15D99E8, owner at glue +4, its slot-1 handler at glue +0x20 = CReorgPanel::OnClose); sets **+0x39 = 1** (needs a fill); makes the window `reorg_window` through the screen's gui (screen slot 14, then its slot 11 with the screen's slot 16) into +0; finds the text boxes `positioning_left` (+0x3C), `positioning_right` (+0x40), `ships_ratio_left` (+0x44) and `ships_ratio_right` (+0x48) (the window's slot 15); finds `closebutton` (slot 13) and registers the glue on it; hides the window and sets **+0x38 = 0** (not shown). It names nothing else: `reorg_label`, `reorg_bg` and `unitname_1`/`_2` are not touched here, and `reorg_label` and `reorg_bg` are named nowhere in the image. Starts abutting the transfer handler's `ret 4` at 0x763D0D with no padding (trap 2). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.1.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x763D10-0x763F4D: `ret 8` at 0x763F4D, `mov edi,[ebp+8]` (this) and `[ebp+0xC]` (the screen, which Enter passes as ebx = the CInGameIdler at 0x65F08A), eax = edi on return. The one caller is 0x65F08C, whose result is stored to idler +0x1358 at 0x65F0AC. The string searches: image.findBytes('reorg_label') and ('reorg_bg') return nothing while 'unitname_2' and 'positioning_right' (positive controls) are found. What would show it wrong: a reference to those element names built at run time from pieces.

addresses.name: CReorgPanel::OnClose
addresses.comment: `closebutton`'s handler (the glue's slot 1). Ignores its receiver and asks the in-game screen (g_CCurrentGameState +0xBE8) for its slot 50, **CInGameIdler::CloseReorganiseWindow** - which closes the window (CReorgPanel_Close) where it is shown. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.6.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x763F50-0x763FFF (`ret 4`): the only reference is the store `mov [esi+0x20], 0x763F50` at 0x763D51 into the panel's glue, whose slot 1 (0x6D3210) jumps to glue+0x20 with ecx = glue+4. The body ends `call [eax+0xC8]` on [g_CCurrentGameState+0xBE8]; 0xC8/4 = 50, and the record has CInGameIdler slot 50 = CloseReorganiseWindow. What would show it wrong: the in-game screen not being a CInGameIdler while the window is up.

addresses.name: CReorgPanel_Update
addresses.comment: **The window's per-frame test, and the only thing that keeps it current.** Asked by CInGameIdler_UpdatePanels (0x650914) every frame the window is shown; answering false closes it. **False exactly where the two units are not in the same province** (CUnit +0x130 of +4 and +8 differ) - nothing else shuts it: no battle, path, retreat or ownership test. Otherwise: `unitname_1` is set to the left unit's full name (CUnit::GetName, slot 7) and `unitname_2` to the right's, **every frame**; then where +0x39 is set, or `left_list`'s row count (the list's slot 10) is not the left unit's regiments_count (+0x40), or the same for `right_list` and the right unit, the window is hidden, **filled again (CReorgPanel_Fill)** and +0x39 cleared. Answers true. So a transfer is shown when the brigade counts change, not when the button is clicked. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.5.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x7646D0-0x764957: the panel arrives in EDI (read at 0x7646E8 before any write), two exits, both bare `ret` - 0x764712 with AL = the low byte cleared, 0x764957 with `mov al,1`. The comparisons are `cmp eax,[ecx+0x130]` at 0x7646F9 and the two `call [edx+0x28]; cmp eax,esi; setne` at 0x764890 and 0x7648F7 against [unit+0x40]. The refill is `mov esi,edi; call 0x764960` at 0x76493C. What would show it wrong: the list's slot 10 answering something other than a row count.

addresses.name: CReorgPanel_Fill
addresses.comment: **Fills both lists and the four fleet figures, and shows the window.** `left_list` gets the rows of the **left unit (+4, the first selected)** from the template `reorg_entry`, each row's target the right unit; `right_list` the rows of the **right unit (+8, the second selected)** from `reorg_entry_right`, each row's target the left unit (CReorgPanel_FillList). Then, **where neither unit is a fleet (CUnit slot 16, IsNaval)**, the four text boxes positioning_left/right and ships_ratio_left/right are hidden (slot 14, byte +0xF4 = 1); otherwise each is written - CReorgPanel::WritePositioning(left, then right) and CReorgPanel_WriteUnitsRatio(left, then right) - and shown (+0xF4 = 0, slot 13). Last the window is shown and +0x38 = 1. Called by CInGameIdler::OnReorganiseButton and CReorgPanel_Update. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, sections A.2 and A.4.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x764960-0x764B8B (bare `ret`): the panel is ESI throughout and the callers set it (0x76493C `mov esi,edi`); `call 0x764d90` at 0x7649E4 with ecx = [esi+4], edx = left_list, the pushed target [esi+8] and the string 'reorg_entry'; at 0x764A67 with ecx = [esi+8], the target [esi+4] and 'reorg_entry_right'. The naval gate is `call [eax+0x40]` on each unit, slot 16 = IsNaval in the record. What would show it wrong: slot 16 not being IsNaval on CArmy/CAir (the tables give ReturnFalse 0x592360 there, CNavy ReturnTrue 0xA92590).

addresses.name: CReorgPanel_FillList
addresses.signature: void __fastcall CReorgPanel_FillList(CUnit* unit@ECX, void* list@EDX, CUnit* target@stack:4, Hoi3CString templateName@stack:8)
addresses.comment: One list: keeps the list's scroll position (its scrollbar +0xF8, slot 4; -1.0 where it has none), builds a row maker {the in-game screen, target, templateName} and hands the unit's brigade list (CUnit +0x38's first node) to CReorgPanel_SyncList, then puts the scrollbar back at (int)floor((position + 0.0005) x 1000) through its slot 7 (value, 1, 1). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.2.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x764D90-0x764F39: `ret 0x20` = the target (4) plus a std::string by value (0x1C); esi = ecx (unit), edi = edx (list) at entry; the maker is [ebp-0x3C] = g_CCurrentGameState+0xBE8, [ebp-0x38] = [ebp+8], a copy of the string at [ebp+0xC] (0x401BD0); `call 0x770210` at 0x764E99 with (list, first node, &maker), cleaned by the caller (add esp,0xC). The constants: 0x170AC0C = -1.0f, 0x160A460 = 0.0005, 0x160A300 = 1000.0. What would show it wrong: the scrollbar's slot 7 taking something other than a position.

addresses.name: CReorgPanel_SyncList
addresses.signature: void __cdecl CReorgPanel_SyncList(void* list, LinkedListNode* firstBrigade, void* maker)
addresses.comment: **Makes a list's rows match a unit's brigades, keeping the rows it can.** Walks the list's rows (its slot 11) and the brigades together: a row whose brigade (CReorgEntry +0x28) is this brigade and whose target (+0x50) is the maker's target is kept; otherwise a later row that matches is moved up to here (0x770860), and failing that a new CReorgEntry(screen, brigade, target, templateName) is inserted before the row (list slot 6). When the rows run out, a new row is appended (slot 4) for each brigade left, at most 128 (0x80) in the pass; when the brigades run out, the rows from there on are removed (slot 24). **So the rows are in the unit's own brigade order (CUnit +0x38)**, and an unchanged row is the same object as before - with the figures it was made with. One caller, CReorgPanel_FillList. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.2.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled (Ghidra, a copy of Hoi3_v12.1.2) and checked against the disassembly of 0x770210-0x7703D9: two bare `ret`s, the callee reading its three arguments off [ebp+8]/[ebp+0xC]/[ebp+0x10]; the comparisons are ResolvePersistentIdInPlace(row+0x28) == brigade and CRef_ResolveAndCache(row+0x50) == maker[1]; both makers `push 0xC8` and call 0x7630F0. The 128 is `cmp 0x80` in the append loop. What would show it wrong: the list slots 4/6/24 not being append/insert/remove - read from their use here only.

addresses.name: CReorgPanel::WritePositioning
addresses.comment: `positioning_left` (left: the left unit, text box +0x3C) or `positioning_right` (the right unit, +0x40): p = NavalStackingPositionPenalty of a one-entry list holding that unit; the text is POSITIONING_PENALTY with VAL = colour + FormatFixedPoint(p, 3) + `%§!`, the colour **§G where p < floor(1.5f) = 1, §R otherwise** - green only at no penalty, since p is never negative. **p is printed as it is, in thousandths, with no x100**: a 5% penalty (50) reads `0.050%`, where the unit panel's `positioning` (CWindowForSubUnitsEntry::Fill) multiplies by 100 first. The 1.5 is the shared literal fAiPowerRatio_1_5 (VA 0x17179AC). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.4.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x764010-0x764232 (`ret 4`, ecx = panel): the one-node list {unit, 0, 0, 0} is built at 0x76404F-0x764085 and `call 0x5d5b80` at 0x764088 with ESI = &p; `movss xmm0,[0x17179ac]; floorf; _ftol2` then `mov esi,0x15b5c58 ('§R'); cmp ecx,eax; jge; mov esi,0x15b5c50 ('§G')`; `push 3; push p; call 0xa5aca0` (FormatFixedPoint) with nothing between the call to the penalty and the format that scales p; AppendLocalisedLine('VAL','POSITIONING_PENALTY'). The unit panel's x100 is `push 0x186a0 ... push 0x3e8` around 0xB99AF0 at 0x754AA3. What would show it wrong: localisation POSITIONING_PENALTY carrying its own scale (it is 'Positioning Penalty: $VAL$').

addresses.name: CReorgPanel_WriteUnitsRatio
addresses.comment: `ships_ratio_left` (left: the left unit, +0x44) or `ships_ratio_right` (+0x48): over the unit's brigades (CUnit +0x38), counting only ships (definition `is_ship`, +0x2E): a transport (`is_transport`, +0x30) is a transport; else a capital (`is_capital`, +0x2F) is a capital; else **anything but a submarine (`is_sub`, +0x31) is a screen - a submarine is counted nowhere**. The text is UNIT_RATIO with RAT = `§G` capitals `§! / §G` screens `§! / §G` transports `§!` - all three green, always. Two heavy cruisers (capital = yes), six light cruisers and a destroyer flotilla give `2 / 7 / 0`; a submarine flotilla alone `0 / 0 / 0`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.4.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x764240-0x7646C0 (`ret 8`, the panel at [ebp+8], the flag at [ebp+0xC]); the loop at 0x76428D-0x7642C0 tests [def+0x2E], then [def+0x30] (inc edi, transports), [def+0x2F] (inc esi, capitals), [def+0x31]; the literals are 0x15B5C50 '§G', 0x15D8250 '§! / §G' and 0x15B5138 '§!'; AppendLocalisedLine('RAT','UNIT_RATIO'). The oracle: the maintainer's screenshot of Schlachtflotte reads 2 / 7 / 0 (Deutschland and Admiral Scheer heavy cruisers, tfh/units/heavy_cruiser.txt capital = yes; five light cruisers, Emden and one destroyer flotilla) and I. Unterseebootsflotte 0 / 0 / 0 (submarine.txt is_sub = yes). What would show it wrong: a fleet with a submarine and a screen reading the submarine into the middle figure.

addresses.name: CReorgPanel_Close
addresses.comment: **Shutting the window.** Hides it; then for each of the two units: **one left with no brigades (+0x40 == 0) is disbanded - a CDisbandCommand(unit) is posted** through the session's command channel; one that still has brigades has its `is_allowed_empty` (+0x159) cleared. +0x38 = 0. Called by CInGameIdler::CloseReorganiseWindow (slot 50, so by closebutton too) and from two other sites (0x663C0B, 0x664386: the row add and remove the record's AddUnitRow/RemoveUnitRow comments describe as 'the reorganise window closed if up'). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.6.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and checked against the disassembly of 0x764B90-0x764D89: the panel in EDI, two bare `ret`s; `cmp [unit+0x40],0` per unit, `push 100; operator new; CDisbandCommand::CDisbandCommand(cmd, unit)`, posted with in_game_screen->GetSession()->+0x38 slot 6, as CReorgEntry::OnTransfer posts; otherwise `mov byte ptr [eax+0x159], bl` at 0x764C89 and 0x764D74. Callers from findRefs --callers 0x764B90: 0x656DFD, 0x663C0B, 0x664386. What would show it wrong: +0x159 being anything but the flag CCreateUnitCommand::Execute copies is_allowed_empty into.

addresses.name: CReorgEntry::CReorgEntry
addresses.signature: CReorgEntry* __stdcall CReorgEntry::CReorgEntry(CReorgEntry* this, CInGameIdler* screen, CSubUnit* brigade, CUnit* target, Hoi3CString* templateName)
addresses.comment: **A row of the reorganise window, made once and never updated** (slot 8 is the empty stub). Makes the row's window from the template (`reorg_entry` or `reorg_entry_right`) through the screen's gui into +0x20; the brigade as a CRef at +0x28, the **target - the unit on the other side, where the brigade would go** - as a CRef at +0x50; the glue CButtonObserverGlue<CReorgEntry> at +0x78 with slot-1 handler CReorgEntry::OnTransfer, registered on `transferbutton`. Then: `subunit_name` = the brigade's name (CSubUnit slot 8, +0x68); `subunit_type` = its definition's name (the definition's slot 6); `subunit_strength` = the brigade's slot 13 - **a brigade's men (CRegiment::StrengthText, FormatMen: strength x 100, cut to a whole man, so 29.996 is `2,999`), a ship's or wing's strength as a whole percentage (CShip::StrengthText, `100%`)**; `subunit_level` = IntToRoman(the index of CHistoricalModel::PickBestModel(the brigade's owner's models of its type, brigade) + 1), **I where there is none**; `counter_type` = the sprite `GFX_counter_` + the definition's key where that sprite exists (else the file's GFX_temp_unit_icon); `counter_size` frame 1; **`org_bar` = (int)(100 x org / max(the definition's max_organisation +0xF0, org))** - the definition's figure, not CSubUnit::GetMaxOrganisation, so no officers, commander or reserve penalty; **`str_bar` = (int)(100 x strength / max(CSubUnit::GetMaxStrength(0,0), strength))**; last, the row's window and its elements are given the group string `<id type>_<id>` of the brigade (the window's +0x18 slot 30, the call that gives the diplomatic icons `diplo_message`). **transferbutton is never disabled or hidden**: nothing in the window asks whether the brigade may go (0xE1010 has no caller in 0x763000-0x765200). `band_reorg_regiment` is not named in the image. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.3.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled (Ghidra, a copy of Hoi3_v12.1.2) and checked against the disassembly: `ret 0x14` at 0x763992 = five dwords; [ebp+8] this (edi), [ebp+0xC] the screen (its slots 16, 14, 17 are the gui calls), [ebp+0x10] the brigade (`[ecx+0x58]+8` at 0x7634E2 for the counter), [ebp+0x14] the target into 0x42DD70(+0x50); the counter lookup is StringHashFind (0x9C7D60) on screen slot 17 +0xA0; the bars' divisors are `[[sub+0x58]+0xF0]` and the brigade's slot 12 (GetMaxStrength) with (out, 0, 0); 100.0 is the double at 0x160A358. findRefs --callers 0x4E1010 lists 0x4850A0, 0x5DCCF3, 0x5EB680, 0x736596, 0x73AAC4 - none in the window's code. Oracle: the save's Leibstandarte has strength=29.996 and the screenshot reads 2,999; Pionier-Bataillon 114 strength=10.000 reads 1,000. What would show it wrong: a later call that re-enables or disables `transferbutton` by name - its string 0x15D2524 has two references, 0x763273 (here) and 0x6C78FA (the idler's tooltip name table).

addresses.name: CReorgEntry::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: Slot 0: CReorgEntry::~CReorgEntry, and free() where flags bit 0 is set. The table at +0x1C reaches it through the two-instruction thunk 0x7726B0 (`sub ecx,0x1c; jmp`).
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x7639A0-0x7639BF: esi = ecx, `push esi; call 0x7639d0`, `test byte ptr [ebp+8],1`, free(esi), eax = esi, `ret 4`. vtable.py: CReorgEntry slot 0 of the table at VA 0x15D9924 is 0x7639A0; slot 0 of the +0x1C table is 0x7726B0, held by that one table only.

addresses.name: CReorgEntry::~CReorgEntry
addresses.comment: The destructor body: the glue at +0x78 back to CButtonObserver's vftable, the two CRefs' names (+0x58 and +0x30 strings) freed, the row's window (+0x20) destroyed through its slot 20, the base tables restored and the list item's base destructor (0xA7F830).
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x7639D0-0x763A80 (`ret 4`, `mov esi,[ebp+8]`): `mov [esi+0x78],0x15b5554`; frees on [esi+0x70]/[esi+0x5C] and [esi+0x48]/[esi+0x34] - the std::string at +0xC of each 0x28-byte CRef; `call [eax+0x50]` on [esi+0x20]. One caller, the slot 0 above.

addresses.name: CReorgEntry::OnTransfer
addresses.comment: **`transferbutton`'s click: send this row's brigade to the unit on the other side.** Resolves the target (CRef +0x50, through the id tables, -8 to the CUnit) and the brigade (CRef +0x28, no -8), caching both; where either is gone, nothing. Otherwise the `click` sound (played unless already playing), and **a CTransferSubUnitCommand(target's id pair - CUnit +0x10/+0x14 -, brigade) is posted** to the session's command channel (in_game_screen slot 18, +0x38, slot 6). No test of its own - whether the move is allowed is the command's (CTransferSubUnitCommand::Execute). **It does not touch the lists**: CReorgPanel_Update fills them again on the next frame where the brigade counts no longer match the rows. One of the command's two interface sites (0x763C53). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.3.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x763A90-0x763D0D (`ret 4`, esi = ecx = the entry): [esi+0x54]/[esi+0x58] -> FindPersistentById, `lea edi,[eax-8]`, stored to [esi+0x50]; [esi+0x2C]/[esi+0x30] -> FindPersistentById, stored to [esi+0x28]; `je 0x763cfc` on either null; sound manager (0xAAC690) slot 25 then slot 9 with 'click'; `push 0x70; operator new`; at 0x763C35-0x763C53 the pushes are the brigade, the 8 bytes [unit+0x10]/[unit+0x14], and the object, then `call 0x5dca90`; the post is [[0x1a89790]+0xBE8] slot 18 -> +0x38 -> slot 6. The only reference to 0x763A90 is the push at 0x7631B3 into the glue constructor in CReorgEntry::CReorgEntry. What would show it wrong: the command's constructor taking its arguments in another order (the record: (this, unitIdType, unitIdSerial, subUnit)).

addresses.name: CRef_ResolveDirect
addresses.comment: CRef_Resolve (0x19A190) **without the -8**: the ref in EAX, its type (+4) and id (+8) looked up in the high or low id table by type > 0x1268 (FindPersistentById), the object answered as found, or 0. For a CRef to an object whose CPersistent is at +0 - a CSubUnit - where CRef_Resolve's -8 is for one reached through CReferenceObject at +8 (a CUnit). Bare `ret`, two exits. 18 direct callers, so class-free; CReorgEntry::CReorgEntry reads its brigade through it.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x806210-0x80624F: `mov ecx,[eax+4]; mov eax,[eax+8]` into a stack key, `cmp ecx,0x1268` choosing [0x1a857f0] or [0x1a857f4], `call 0xa9da00` and straight to the epilogue with no `add eax,-8`; the null-table exit `xor eax,eax`. findRefs --callers 0x806210: 18 direct calls; vtable.py --holding: in no table. What would show it wrong: a caller handing it a CRef to a CUnit and using the answer as a CUnit.

addresses.name: CShip::StrengthText
addresses.comment: Slot 13 of CShip and CWing (CSubUnit's slot 13 is pure; CRegiment's is CRegiment::StrengthText): **the strength as a whole percentage** - FormatFixedPoint(strength +0x5C, 0 decimals) + `%`, so a ship at 100.000 reads `100%`. What the reorganise window's `subunit_strength` shows for a ship where a brigade shows men.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0x5ADD80 and checked: `ret 4` at 0x5ADE78; FormatFixedPoint(out, [this+0x5C], 0) then operator+ with the literal '%'. vtable.py --holding 0x5ADD80: CShip slot 13 and CWing slot 13, nothing else; CSubUnit slot 13 is _purecall 0xB961D5. The oracle: every ship in the maintainer's fleet screenshot reads 100%.

addresses.name: CReorgWindow_ElementTooltip
addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __stdcall CReorgWindow_ElementTooltip(CReorgPanel* window, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element) @EAX
addresses.comment: The reorganise window's (idler +0x1358) tooltip. **Where either unit is a fleet** (CUnit slot 16) and the element is ships_ratio_left or _right (+0x44, +0x48): REORG_WND_SHIPS_RATIO_DESC 'Ratio of Capitals/Screens/Transports'. Otherwise the row of `left_list`, then of `right_list`, that owns the element (the row's +0x1C table, slot 22) answers with its brigade's CSubUnit_SummaryTooltip (0x5A9900) - **so `transferbutton` says the brigade's summary, not TRANSFER_SUB**. Anything else - closebutton, the positioning lines, the names, the label - gets an empty tooltip. CInGameIdler::GetElementTooltip asks this first whenever the window is shown (+0x38) and holds the element (0x6C5392..0x6C53E1), and takes its answer whatever it is, so the screen's own `closebutton` CLOSE and `transferbutton` TRANSFER_SUB are never reached from inside this window. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md, section A.7, and FINDINGS-unitpaneltooltips.md, section 1.
addresses.evidence: Revised: the first argument's type (void* -> CReorgPanel*, the struct this fragment declares) and the comment - the naval gate, the empty answer and what it hides. Decompiled 0x764F40 (Ghidra copy): the ratio branch is behind `slot 16 of [window+4] || slot 16 of [window+8]`; the fall-through copies an empty GuiTooltipText to out (0x7651E3). In GetElementTooltip the call at 0x6C53D4 is followed by `jmp 0x6c9450`, the common exit that only positions the result, with no test of it being empty; the name table that holds closebutton and transferbutton (0x6C78F9 'transferbutton' -> TRANSFER_SUB) is further down. `ret 0xC` at 0x76520B. What would show it wrong: the tooltip box falling back to another source on an empty text.

struct_fields.name: window
struct_fields.comment: The `reorg_window` window, made by the constructor through the screen's gui.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov [edi], eax` at 0x763DBA after the gui's slot 11 with 'reorg_window'; every element lookup goes through [panel] (slots 13, 15, 31).

struct_fields.name: left_unit
struct_fields.comment: The first selected unit (CInGameIdler::OnReorganiseButton), the one whose brigades are in `left_list` and whose name is `unitname_1`.
struct_fields.evidence: Written by OnReorganiseButton from selection.first; read as the unit of left_list (0x7649DF), unitname_1 (slot 7) in CReorgPanel_Update and the left positioning/ratio.

struct_fields.name: right_unit

struct_fields.name: window

struct_fields.name: brigade
struct_fields.comment: The brigade the row shows and would send, a CRef (pointer, id type +0x2C, id +0x30, name +0x34) to a CSubUnit - resolved without CRef_Resolve's -8.
struct_fields.evidence: Built by 0x7C9530(this+0x28, brigade) at 0x763194; OnTransfer resolves [+0x2C]/[+0x30] with no -8 and caches at +0x28; CReorgPanel_SyncList and the tooltip resolve it with ResolvePersistentIdInPlace.

struct_fields.name: target
struct_fields.comment: The unit the brigade would go to - the window's other unit - a CRef to a CUnit (resolved with the -8).
struct_fields.evidence: Built by 0x42DD70(this+0x50, target) at 0x7631A5 (the constructor's fourth argument, the maker's target); OnTransfer resolves [+0x54]/[+0x58], `lea edi,[eax-8]`, caches at +0x50, and hands its +0x10/+0x14 to the command.

struct_fields.name: transfer_observer
struct_fields.comment: CButtonObserverGlue<CReorgEntry> by value, 0x50 bytes (to the end of the row): vftable VA 0x15D99BC, owner at +0x7C, the slot-1 handler CReorgEntry::OnTransfer at +0xB0; registered on `transferbutton`.
struct_fields.evidence: The glue constructor 0x76FBA0 is called with EAX = edi+0x78 and ecx = edi (0x7631C7-0x7631CC), the handler 0x763A90 its 13th pushed argument, written to EAX[0xE]; the glue's slot 1 (0x813D80) jumps to [glue+0x38] with ecx = [glue+4] + [glue+0x3C].

struct_fields.name: is_allowed_empty
struct_fields.comment: Whether the unit may stand with no brigades: CCreateUnitCommand::Execute copies the command's is_allowed_empty here, and CUnit::UpdateHourly acts on a unit with regiments_count 0 only while it is clear (0x5BA011). The reorganise window's close clears it on each of its units that still has brigades and disbands the one that has none. The name follows the command's, which is inference from its LoadKey list.
struct_fields.evidence: fieldchain --field 0x159: on a CUnit, the writes at 0x764C89/0x764D74 (CReorgPanel_Close, [panel+4]/[panel+8]), 0x5B51BE (CUnit::CUnit) and 0x5EBA9E; the reads at 0x5BA011 (UpdateHourly, beside `cmp [esi+0x40], ebx`). The record's CCreateUnitCommand::Execute comment: 'CUnit +0x159 from +0x59'. The other hits of the bare displacement are gui objects or stack slots (0x769E30 is CUnitView's edit box). What would show it wrong: UpdateHourly's empty-unit branch reading it for some other purpose.

struct_fields.name: reorganise_window
struct_fields.comment: The reorganise window, a CReorgPanel (0x4C bytes) made once by Enter: given two units and shown by OnReorganiseButton (+4, +8, byte +0x39), shown flag +0x38, kept current by CReorgPanel_Update and closed by slot 50 (CReorgPanel_Close); asked first by GetElementTooltip (FINDINGS-reorgwindow.md section A).
struct_fields.evidence: Revised: the type, void* -> CReorgPanel* (declared here), and the comment names the functions. Enter stores the result of CReorgPanel::CReorgPanel here at 0x65F0AC.
